title: Genitives in theological prose
subtitle: State the relationship before making an interpretive choice.
overview: Theological prose often compresses meaning into genitive phrases. “Of” is only a first gloss; the relationship may be source, possession, description, object, or subject.
When more than one reading is possible, record the alternatives and look to sentence and paragraph context before deciding.

sections.title: Relationship questions
rows: God’s love / love for God; context decides
glory belonging to / associated with God
word characterized by or concerning life

items.grc: ἡ ἀγάπη τοῦ θεοῦ ἐκκέχυται ἐν ταῖς καρδίαις ἡμῶν.
items.en: The love of God has been poured into our hearts; establish the relationship from context.

items.grc: διὰ πίστεως Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ εἰς πάντας τοὺς πιστεύοντας.
items.en: Through faith of/in Jesus Christ for all who believe; note the interpretive question carefully.
